clue.text: A different f-frock or a different house?

definitions.meaning: a change of a dress, with the stammered f- turning 'a dress' into 'of address'
moving to a new home means a new postal address

explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'f-frock' is a playful nudge: a change of a dress, said with an extra F, becomes the postal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving house gives you a new postal location, the phrase used when notifying people of a move.

clue.text: One needs to iron top half of kilt for socialising later

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
to iron clothes is to press them

indicators.note: the first half of the word kilt is taken, its top in a down entry

explanation.surface: Someone has to press half a kilt before a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top half of' takes KI, the first two letters of 'kilt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the drinking and partying that follows a day on the slopes, socialising after skiing.

clue.text: Move left foot in this game

parts.note: to move is to go

explanation.surface: In this sport you shift your left foot as you play.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a game played with clubs and balls on a course.

clue.text: Light cannon is area of interest to assassin

parts.note: one's field is one's area of interest or expertise
a gun is slang for a hired gunman or assassin

explanation.surface: A small artillery piece is what a hitman specialises in.
explanation.definitionFit: A field gun is a light, mobile artillery piece used in the field rather than in a fort.

clue.text: Lion eats worker in outbuilding

indicators.note: the lion swallows the worker, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Leo is the Lion of the zodiac
an ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A lion devours a labourer inside a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed or outbuilding propped against a wall.

clue.text: Horror is stated to be spurious

indicators.note: spurious means false, so these letters are not genuine and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fear said to be groundless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spurious' rearranges the eight letters of 'is stated'; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is strong dislike or revulsion, a mild form of horror.

clue.text: Wool untangled in Rome

indicators.note: untangling reorders the strands, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Yarn being sorted out in the Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Merino is fine wool from the Merino breed of sheep.

clue.text: Controlled by the computer stealthily?

parts.note: a counter can be one who computes; something sold furtively is passed beneath the shop's serving surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'computer' is read as 'one who counts', a counter, playing on the idiom for illicit sales.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes goods sold secretly or illegally, passed beneath the shop's serving surface.

clue.text: Entrance concealed by this peony

indicators.note: the target word is disguised within a rearrangement of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A trance is hidden in this garden flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE), not a doorway. 'concealed' signals a rearrangement of 'this peony'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to put them in a trance, to mesmerise them.

clue.text: "John holds me" — this leads to correction or clarification

definitions.text: this leads to correction or clarification

indicators.note: John holds me, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: Ian is the Scottish form of John

explanation.surface: A man named John embraces the speaker, prompting a clarification.
explanation.definitionFit: Speakers say this little phrase to introduce a correction or to clarify what they just said.

clue.text: Flue with end restored is required

indicators.note: restoring rebuilds the parts in new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chimney with its end rebuilt is a necessity.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful is an adjective meaning necessary or required.

clue.text: Beastly remark about start of NHS

indicators.note: the remark goes around the next piece

parts.note: to remark is to notice

indicators.note: the first letter of NHS is taken

explanation.surface: A nasty comment about how the health service began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes N from NHS (Britain's National Health Service), which goes inside NOTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beastly in British informal use means unpleasant or mean, the same as not nice.

clue.text: Pleased to show freedom from pain

indicators.note: the word Pleased displays the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A patient happy to be pain-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is comfort, the absence of pain or discomfort.

clue.text: Fair dealer keeps merchandise in a haven

indicators.note: the haven holds the merchandise, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a port is a haven for ships
goods are merchandise

explanation.surface: An honest trader stores stock in a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A good sport is a fair-minded person who plays or deals fairly.

clue.text: Friday's child makes you shiver

parts.note: Fri is the short form of Friday, plus the possessive S
a son is a child

explanation.surface: The child born on a Friday gives you the shivers.
explanation.walkthrough: Echoes the rhyme 'Monday's child is fair of face'; 'makes you' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a sudden thrill or shiver of excitement.

clue.text: Told to go, having got off floor

parts.note: sent is slang for thrilled, as if high, having got off on something
to floor someone is to knock them down

explanation.surface: Someone ordered away after getting up off the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a student 'sent down' is expelled from university.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent down means dismissed or expelled, especially from a university, or jailed.

clue.text: Introduction in front of the clock

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before or in front of
clock is slang for a person's face

explanation.surface: A prelude placed before the dial of a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A preface is the introduction at the start of a book.

clue.text: Crowd fight in place set aside for reporters

parts.note: to crowd is to press
to box is to fight

explanation.surface: A crowd brawls in the area kept for journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: A press box is the reserved area at a sports ground where journalists sit.

clue.text: A funny joke, one worked out about love affair

annotationWithheld.why: A funny joke, one worked out about love affair (1,4,3): the only parse found, A + GONE round O + OD, needs 'about' both as container and to turn DO; no reading supplies the G otherwise
annotationWithheld.clue: A funny joke, one worked out about love affair

clue.text: Devalued car, wrecked outside

indicators.note: the wrecked word goes around the car

parts.note: dished in British informal use means ruined
a Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A small car's value plunges after a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminished means reduced or lessened in value or worth.

clue.text: Deplores our name being in paper

indicators.note: our name sits inside the paper

parts.note: MS is manuscript, a paper

explanation.surface: Someone laments seeing our name printed in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To mourn something is to grieve over it, close to deploring it.

clue.text: Chopped capers in pickle

indicators.note: chopping cuts things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe step: cut-up capers in a preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' means a predicament, not a preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament, the same as being in a pickle.

clue.text: Tramp has nothing on top of the cooker

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the hob is the flat top of a cooker
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A vagrant with an empty pan on the stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is an American word for a tramp or homeless wanderer.

clue.text: Returning officer initially gets down to run

indicators.note: the first letters of these two words are taken

parts.note: down here means beneath, under

explanation.surface: An election official first has to bring the numbers down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes R and O; 'gets' and 'to' are links. In rounders, a British bat-and-ball game, a rounder is a run.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounder is the scoring run in the game of rounders.

clue.text: Understudy is nearly permanent

indicators.note: nearly means almost all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: standing means permanent, as in a standing order

explanation.surface: The understudy is practically a fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the final G of STANDING.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute, as an understudy is for an actor.

clue.text: One driving test reversing a bit

parts.note: one is A

indicators.note: the test is read backwards, as a car reverses

parts.note: the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars

explanation.surface: Someone takes a driving test and reverses a little.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is a tiny particle, so a bit or iota.

clue.text: Fermented wines strengthen, as poets say

indicators.note: fermenting works changes, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poets claim fermented wine makes you stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as poets say' marks the verb use as poetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To sinew, in poetic use, is to strengthen as if with tendons.

clue.text: Say, perhaps I will be going to church

parts.note: I is an example of a pronoun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A speaker announces they are heading to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be going to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to say or articulate a word.
